🇺🇸 Pentagon expands F-35 orders, signaling potential military buildup
The Pentagon has struck a 10-year deal with Lockheed Martin for the production of 850 F-35 stealth fighter jets.
While neither of the sides specified a value for the agreement, the F-35 versions could cost over $100 million per plane.
Air & Space Forces Magazine reported the following production costs in September 2026:
🔴 F-35A – $92 million
🔴 F-35B – $121.4 million
🔴 F-35C – $110.8 million
Using the average price, 850 aircraft would cost approximately $91.8 billion. In addition to F-35s, the agreement also includes "initial spares, ten years of modification kits and sustainment, and international customer orders," according to Lockheed. The Pentagon’s framework agreement still requires congressional approval.
The F-35 program has repeatedly faced criticism from US lawmakers over cost overruns, delays, and hardware and software flaws. During the war with Iran, one F-35 was heavily damaged in March. In July, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) stated that it had destroyed three F-35s and damaged another three during a ballistic missile attack on Al-Azraq Air Base in Jordan.

events.text:
🇺🇸📉🇮🇱 Israel Lobby’s New Playbook: From Buying Politicians to Targeting Critics
Nearly 20 years after John Mearsheimer and Stephen Walt shook up American politics with The Israel Lobby and U.S. Foreign Policy, a new book reveals how much has changed.
In Israel’s Lobby, Eli Clifton and Ian Lustick trace a lobbying network that has grown considerably richer, expanded its influence over US elections and increasingly turned to pressuring critics — even as most Americans now view Israel unfavorably.
Growth in the Influence and Wealth of the Lobby
The authors trace how the lobby’s leading institutions grew wealthier, with AIPAC’s assets rising roughly ninefold between 2000 and 2023. That financial muscle reaches directly into elections: AIPAC said its members had given over $53M to pro-Israel candidates during the 2024 cycle by early November.
Two court rulings in 2010 helped build the machinery, opening the way for super PACs to raise and spend unlimited sums independently of candidates. Direct campaign donations remain capped, but wealthy donors can fund waves of ads against a critic. AIPAC credited its affiliated United Democracy Project with helping defeat Jamaal Bowman and Cori Bush in Democratic primaries, giving other lawmakers a concrete reason to fear crossing it.
Change in Israel’s Policy
Clifton and Lustick argue that this growing financial strength has accompanied Israel’s retreat from a negotiated settlement with the Palestinians toward military dominance. The lobby’s task has become harder as Israeli policy leaves less room for the peace promises that once helped sell US support.
Their account also describes a move from defending Israel’s actions to treating opposition as antisemitism, with pressure extending into universities and public debate. When criticism carries a risk to careers, funding or reputations, supporters of Israeli policy gain another way to discourage dissent without winning the argument.
Decline in Popularity and New Challenges
Despite that pressure, Pew’s March 2026 survey found that 60% of Americans viewed Israel unfavorably, including majorities under 50 in both parties. The lobby’s deeper pockets have not stopped public opinion from turning, leaving a widening gap between what many Americans think and the choices their leaders make.
The US war against Iran shows how easily “America First” rhetoric can coexist with military action sought by Israel. For Palestinians and countries facing Israeli attacks, falling approval ratings offer little protection while political backing and weapons keep flowing. Public anger becomes a material constraint only when it changes those decisions.

🇶🇦🇺🇸🛢 Qatari US LNG deal highlights windfall for American gas producers amid the Hormuz crisis
QatarEnergy has signed two long-term agreements with US energy company Cheniere to purchase up to 4 million tons of liquefied natural gas (LNG) annually through 2054.
According to QatarEnergy, the agreements cover LNG supplies from Cheniere’s Sabine Pass facility in Louisiana and Corpus Christi facility in Texas. Deliveries are expected to begin in 2031 and continue through 2054. The move shows Qatar’s efforts to diversify its LNG supply sources beyond the Gulf and reduce reliance on shipments from the region.
Qatar has long been one of the world’s largest LNG exporters. Before the US-Israeli war against Iran, the Gulf region – primarily Qatar – accounted for roughly 20% of global LNG exports. During the conflict, QatarEnergy’s facilities at Ras Laffan Industrial City and Mesaieed Industrial City were hit, knocking out around 17% of Qatar’s total LNG production capacity. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz further restricted [Qatar’s export options](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76289).
As a result, QatarEnergy's profit fell by roughly 70% to $4 billion in the first half of 2026. Global credit rating agency Fitch still considers the company reliable, but its outlook remains negative, meaning a downgrade is still possible.
👉 While Donald Trump has repeatedly called on Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, US LNG companies continue to benefit from the price spikes and gas shortages caused by the crisis. They had previously reaped huge profits by filling the gap left by declining Russian gas supplies to Europe following US-backed sanctions on Russia and [the Nord Stream sabotage](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/69080).

Ansar Allah started targeting Aramco facilities in August, ramping up strikes in September in a bid to put economic pressure on the world’s #1 crude oil exporter to force it to end its decade-long war and blockade of Yemen.

🚨🇮🇷 Iran vows to unveil ‘Father of All Bombs’ amid Trump’s MOAB threats
 
“The quantity of our missiles has grown at least 1.5 times since before the 12-Day War. Their quality has improved tremendously; their range, destructive power, and accuracy have increased. The United States has used its ‘Mother of All Bombs’. We are preparing to unveil the ‘Father of All Bombs’, something new to the enemy,” IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebi has said.
👉 Reiterating that Hormuz is “100% closed” to US warships, and that commercial vessels have resorted to smuggling in the dead of night with their transponders turned off, Mohebi pointed to evasive maneuvers carrier groups had to make in the course of the 2026 war as a sign of US awareness of the capabilities of Iran’s missiles, not all of which have been unveiled.
It’s not clear what sort of weapon Iran may unveil to compete with the Mother of All Bombs, whose gravity drop, air burst GBU-43B variant has a ~11 tons of TNT yield. The related GBU-57 MOP bunker buster has a ~2.4-ton TNT equivalent yield, and is optimized for kinetic penetration.[ Iran’s Khorramshahr-4 ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/66835)comes closest in terms of payload (1.8k kg) and can be equipped with cluster bomblets to overwhelm enemy defenses.
➡️ Until now, Iran has generally not tried to match US capabilities weapon-for-weapon, but instead stuck to an asymmetric strategy of inexpensive, mass-produced missiles and drones shielded in underground ‘missile cities’, and leveraged its geographic control of the Hormuz Strait. [The big exception is Fattah-1 and 2](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/51952) – Iran’s lineup of hypersonic missiles. The US has yet to field a comparable capability.

🇮🇱 Israel insists war is peace’s only path, warns Hamas is poised to strike again
The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) has briefed US military and Israeli government officials on an intelligence assessment asserting that Hamas is gearing up to resume fighting in the Gaza Strip, Haaretz reports.
👉 The Israeli report argued that disarming the group would require a return to military action, asserting that an international body – an apparent reference to Donald Trump’s Board of Peace – would be unable to accomplish the task.
The IDF also said that Hamas had repaired its tunnel network, replenished its weapons stockpiles in areas of the Gaza Strip still under its control, and rebuilt its ranks to an estimated 30,000-40,000 operatives, roughly matching its strength before October 7, 2023.
🔊Haaretz noted that the assessment emerged amid the Netanyahu government’s reluctance to cooperate with the Gaza peace plan.
The report also comes just five days before Israel’s October 27 general election, in which Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is seeking another term as prime minister amid his ongoing corruption trial.
➡️Similar claims by the IDF regarding Hamas’s purported plans were reported by Israeli media on August 23. Earlier that month, Netanyahu rejected a 15-point peace proposal put forward by Trump’s Board of Peace in July, stalling efforts to advance its implementation.
Despite the declared ceasefire, Israel has obstructed progress toward reconstruction in the Gaza Strip while maintaining its blockade. 🚀 Houthi missile and drone blitz targets Saudi MoD HQ, Aramco, two airports
 
Yemen’s Ansar Allah-aligned Armed Forces have resumed strikes on the Saudi interior after a brief pause, announcing ballistic missile and drone attacks on:
🌏 the Ministry of Defense building in Riyadh, saying they scored a “direct hit”
🌏 the King Fahd International Airport in Damman, eastern Saudi Arabia, resulting in “a disruption of air traffic”
🌏 a Saudi Aramco facility in Yanbu, a major industrial and port hub on the Red Sea home to multiple refineries, and the terminus of the East-West oil pipeline. The Armed Forces reported a “direct hit…leading to a fire breaking out at the targeted site”
🌏 the Abha International Airport in southwest Saudi Arabia, also reporting a direct hit on the target
 
The Armed Forces warned “that the Saudi enemy’s threats to target Yemeni tribes will not go unpunished, and if it is involved in carrying out this threat, the consequences it faces will be catastrophic and unexpected, and we will resort to major options that we did not want to take.”
The statement said Saudi air and missile strikes have attacked Yemen over 2.9k times since the July escalation, “targeting civilian infrastructure…committing dozens of crimes and leaving more than 562 martyrs and wounded, most of them women and children.”
Thursday’s statement comes amid reports that non-emergency US Embassy personnel and their families have been ordered to evacuate Saudi Arabia, and viral claims that some members of the kingdom’s political and economic elite may have fled, while top leaders are shuttled from palace to palace to avoid [being targeted by the Houthis](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76522).

🇮🇱 Israel reportedly flies warplanes to Iran’s border to rile Tehran, provoke escalation
 
“Dozens” of IAF fighter jets and tankers were secretly scrambled for a “power projection” mission on Monday, some flying up to the Iranian border before turning back, Israeli and US officials have told Axios.
👉 The mission, taking place the same day Benjamin Netanyahu met with Defense Secretary Hegseth at Ovda Air Base in southern Israel, involved the presumably unauthorized passage of Israeli warplanes through Syrian and Iraqi airspace.
US sources said Israel was aware Iran’s air defenses would inevitably “detect the sortie,” and may have been “hoping the Iranians would fire at the aircraft, providing a justification” for new strikes. The US was notified ahead of time.
➡️ The reported provocation may explain why Iran has activated [‘Mosaic Defense’ ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76600)[– the decentralized defense doctrine](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/65841) which allowed it to survive February’s decapitation strikes and immediately strike back, blinding US air defenses and intelligence and undermining its regional power projection capabilities.
Officials have told Israeli media that[ Israel’s October 27 elections](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76559), in which Netanyahu’s coalition faces a significant chance of losing power, may be postponed if Israel goes into a state of emergency caused by renewed fighting with Iran.
🔊 Opposition leader Yair Lapid has warned Netanyahu that “there is absolutely no reason to attack Iran or anywhere else” before the vote. “It won’t help him in the elections, either, so I don’t understand why he is doing it.”
Netanyahu told Israeli media on Thursday tha[t Iran was a “cancer” ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76605)and that Israel wouldn’t stop attacking until it “brings down” the “regime.”
